name: Is it worth upgrading pool equipment during a remodel?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth upgrading pool equipment during a remodel?
mainEntity.text: Is it worth upgrading pool equipment during a remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upgrading equipment during a remodel is often the most efficient time to do it because the pool is already drained, exposed, and being worked on. Pumps, filters, heaters, automation, lights, and valves can be replaced or improved without reopening the finished pool later. That reduces labor duplication and helps integrate mechanical changes with the overall design. This is especially useful in Los Angeles, where older pools often have outdated equipment that is noisy, inefficient, or harder to maintain. Newer systems can lower operating costs, improve water quality, and make the pool easier to manage day to day. If the remodel already includes plumbing or electrical work, it is usually smarter to address equipment at the same time. Homeowners should ask which equipment is near end of life and whether replacement now prevents future demolition. Not every component must be changed, but equipment upgrades are often a strong value decision during a remodel because they improve both performance and long-term maintenance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, upgrading pool equipment during a remodel is often worth it because the pool is already drained and accessible. Replacing old pumps, filters, heaters, lights, or automation can improve efficiency, reduce repairs, and prevent a second round of demolition later. It is usually more cost-effective than doing the work separately.
